newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BLUES FIRE COACH/GENERAL MANAGER KEENAN AND TEAM PRESIDENT.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BLUES FIRE COACH/GENERAL MANAGER KEENAN AND TEAM PRESIDENT.

text.p: The St Louis Blues dismantled their front office on Thursday, firing head coach and general manager Mike Keenan and president Jack Quinn in a costly rearrangement of the leadership of the NHL club.

Keenan, who was engaged in a bitter feud with superstar Brett Hull, the lone remaining star from the players he inherited from the 1993-94 playoff team, had steered the under-performing Blues to a 15-17-1 mark so far this season.
In his time with the Blues, Keenan compiled a 75-66-22 record.
St Louis may have to eat $7 million left on Keenan's $2 million per-year deal, which has 3 1/2 years remaining.

The Blues moved executive vice president Ron Caron back to the position where he was before Keenan arrived, general manager, and promoted associate coach Jimmy Roberts to replace Keenan behind the bench -- both on an interim basis.
Quinn was replaced by former St Louis Cardinals and Pittsburgh Pirates president Mark Sauer.
Keenan left the New York Rangers on a contractural technicality to join the Blues after coaching New York for just once season, but he brought them the Stanley Cup in 1994 to end a 54-year drought.
In 11-plus seasons as an NHL head coach, the control-conscious, 48-year-old Keenan is 470-318-99.

He started as Philadelphia Flyers coach in 1984-85 and took over the Chicago Blackhawks after four seasons. He stopped coaching Chicago following the 1991-92 campaign and guided the Rangers to the Stanley Cup in 1993-94.

Keenan has a 91-69 career record in the playoffs, having made the postseason in all 11 seasons. He took the Flyers to the Finals in 1985 and 1987, and got the Blackhawks there in 1992, but never won the Cup until going to New York.
The rumour mill already has Keenan headed to Toronto, where the struggling Maple Leafs lead the league in losses under first-year coach Mike Murphy.
Caron was general manager from 1983-94. In 1986, St Louis was a 2-1 loser to the Calgary Flames in Game Seven of the conference finals.
Roberts was named associate coach on July 17 after two seasons as head coach and general manager of the Blues minor league affiliate in the American Hockey League.

Roberts has been an NHL head coach before. He sat behind the bench for the Buffalo Sabres for 45 games in 1981-82 and coached the Hartford Whalers in 1991-92. He also has been an assistant coach with the Sabres and the Pittsburgh Penguins.
As an NHL defenceman/forward for 15 seasons, Roberts played for the Blues and Montreal Candiens, garnering five Stanley Cup rings.
